text:
Olivia Chen: Quick sync — we need to lock the e2e validation gate for cloud partner templates. Current ask from marketplace: templates + TF modules must pass a lightweight end-to-end run before we publish. Who owns the policy and tests?
Raj Patel: I can lead the gating policy. Main questions: what counts as e2e pass? terraform init/apply on a tiny cluster? integration smoke for auth?
Maria Gomez: Proposal: three checks: 1) terraform fmt/validate, 2) terraform apply against a small test account (destroy after), 3) healthcheck that a sample inference flow returns 200 and correct schema.
Jake Lin: Agree. For TF apply we should use a shared sandbox project per partner to avoid quota surprises. We have a script to bootstrap tiny infra.
Olivia Chen: +1. Let's also require a manifest in the repo: /ci/e2e-policy.yaml with meta fields: owner, allowed-regions, required-tests. That way marketplace automation can read it.
Emily Park: Can we standardize the healthcheck for inference? e.g., POST /predict with model=redwood-lite and ensure response contains "tokens" and status 200. Partners can opt out if they provide their own sample.
Raj Patel: Sounds good. I'll draft the policy. Fields: owner, contact, required_tests (list), timeout_mins, allowed_regions. We'll add an approval step for first publish.
Maria Gomez: DevOps note — pipeline should run the following snippet for TF validation:
```yaml
name: partner-e2e-check
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: terraform fmt
        run: terraform fmt -check -diff
      - name: terraform init
        run: terraform init -backend=false
      - name: terraform validate
        run: terraform validate
  apply-smoke:
    needs: validate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: run apply in sandbox
        run: ./ci/run-sandbox-apply.sh --project ${{ secrets.SANDBOX_PROJECT }}
```
Jake Lin: For the sandbox apply script, ensure it supports a dry-run flag and enforces resource caps. Put resource caps in /ci/resource-limits.json.
DevOps Bot: Pipeline created: https://ci.redwood-internal/partner-e2e-checks/1738887654 — triggers on PR to /templates/* and /modules/* :white_check_mark:
Emily Park: Tests for the inference healthcheck: short python snippet we can recommend in README:
```python
import requests
resp = requests.post('https://sandbox.redwood.ai/predict', json={'model':'redwood-lite','prompt':'ping'})
assert resp.status_code == 200
assert 'tokens' in resp.json()
```
Olivia Chen: Great. Next steps: Raj to draft the e2e-policy.yaml schema by EOD Friday. Maria/Jake to add pipeline + sandbox script. Emily to write the suggested healthcheck snippet and add to template README. I'll coordinate with Partnerships PM to inform partner devs about the new checks.
Raj Patel: Will do. I'll post a PR link once the schema is ready.
Maria Gomez: I'll incubate the sandbox project and add resource-limits.json.
Jake Lin: I'll add the apply script and a dry-run mode.
Emily Park: I'll add healthcheck docs and a small unit test harness for partners to run locally.
Olivia Chen: Thanks all — ping me if you hit permission/blockers. Plan to announce gating policy in the partner onboarding doc next week. :eyes:
